extracted.intended_audience: users of Magma and students/researchers in coding theory who are implementing and analysing error-correcting codes
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and API-level semantics (Magma) for constructing new codes from existing ones, analysing weight distributions, applying group actions, computing automorphism/equivalence/isomorphism, and encoding/decoding procedures including syndrome and Euclidean algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Even-weight codewords / ExpurgateCode
rubrics_metrics.description: For binary codes, an important characteristic is parity (whether weight is odd or even). ExpurgateCode(C) returns the code which contains only those codewords of C which are even.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even-weight codewords are preserved under linear combination; use ExpurgateCode to obtain a subcode in which every word is even (example: h4exp).

rubrics_metrics.name: ExtendCode (add parity-check digit)
rubrics_metrics.description: ExtendCode(C) forms a code by adding an overall parity check digit to each word of a binary code, making all words even.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the minimum weight d is odd, the new code will be an [n+1, k, d+1] code. The generator matrix is the old one with a column added so each generator codeword has even parity (example: h4ext).

rubrics_metrics.name: AugmentCode (include all-ones vector)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a binary linear code C does not contain the all-ones vector then AugmentCode(C) returns a larger linear code which contains C together with the all-ones vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many binary Hamming codes already contain the all-ones vector; apply to duals or other codes when appropriate (example: dualh4aug).

rubrics_metrics.name: LengthenCode (augment then extend)
rubrics_metrics.description: LengthenCode(C) performs AugmentCode followed by ExtendCode in one step: it augments C with the all-ones vector and then extends with a parity-check digit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to ExtendCode(AugmentCode(C)); useful shorthand for the combined transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: DirectSum / PlotkinSum / DirectProduct constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: DirectSum(C,D) produces codewords u|v (u ∈ C, v ∈ D). PlotkinSum(C,D) produces u|u+v. DirectProduct(C,D) produces code generated by the Kronecker product of the generator matrices of C and D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These standard algebraic constructions allow building larger codes from smaller ones (example: Reed–Muller code via successive Plotkin sums).

rubrics_metrics.name: PunctureCode (coordinate deletion)
rubrics_metrics.description: PunctureCode(C, i) deletes the ith component of each codeword of C; PunctureCode(C, S) deletes components indexed by S ⊆ {1..n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Puncturing can produce codes equivalent to classical ones (example: puncturing extended Golay yields unextended Golay up to isomorphism); equality vs equivalence/isomorphism distinctions matter (use IsIsomorphic to test equivalence).

rubrics_metrics.name: ShortenCode (select zero coordinate then delete)
rubrics_metrics.description: ShortenCode(C, i) selects only codewords with zero in the ith component and then deletes that component. ShortenCode(C, S) shortens in multiple coordinates S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortening differs from puncturing because it imposes a zero constraint before deletion (example: shortening Ham(2,11) in positions {1,2}).

rubrics_metrics.name: SubfieldSubcode / Subfield restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a code C over field K and subfield S of K, SubfieldSubcode(C,S) returns (i) the code consisting of those words of C whose components are in S and (ii) the restriction map. SubfieldSubcode(C) with no S uses the prime subfield of K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to obtain codes over smaller fields or the prime subfield; provides the restriction mapping for components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum distance as key invariant
rubrics_metrics.description: The most important invariant of a code C is its minimum distance. In a linear code this corresponds to the minimum weight of codewords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Hamming weight is the number of non-zero components. Determination of minimum weight can be computationally expensive (except for some classes like cyclic codes where more efficient algorithms exist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight distribution and computational cost
rubrics_metrics.description: WeightDistribution(C) returns counts of codewords of each weight as sequence of tuples <weight, number>. Calculating the complete weight distribution requires enumerating all codewords up to scalars and is much more expensive than finding the minimum weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MinimumWeight/MinimumDistance are generally expensive; WeightDistribution returns a sequence <wi, ni> with ni>0. For cyclic codes larger sizes may be tractable thanks to special algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: WeightEnumerator / CompleteWeightEnumerator
rubrics_metrics.description: WeightEnumerator(C) returns a polynomial in two indeterminates x,y whose coefficient of x^i y^{n-i} is the number of codewords of weight i. CompleteWeightEnumerator(C) generalises this to q indeterminates for GF(q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two methods for naming indeterminates are shown; WeightEnumerator(C,u) and CompleteWeightEnumerator(C,u) provide enumerators for cosets C+u. MacWilliamsTransform can convert between distributions of a hypothetical code and its dual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group actions on codes: permutation vs monomial
rubrics_metrics.description: There are permutation actions (coordinate permutations of degree n) and monomial actions (coordinate permutations combined with multiplication by non-zero field elements with degree n(q−1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For binary codes (q=2) monomial action reduces to permutation action. Use c^g or Image(g,c) to compute images; degree mismatch yields an error. The image of a code under permutation is isomorphic; under monomial is equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monomial permutation representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A monomial permutation of monomial degree n may be represented as a permutation on the Cartesian product of non-zero field elements and coordinate indices; it is determined by its action on (1,i) and numbering pairs by (q−1)(i−1)+α to represent as degree (q−1)n permutation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This representation is required to express monomial actions as permutations in Magma; only some elements describe monomial permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image and Image(C,g) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: For vector c and group element g, c^g or Image(g,c) returns the image under permutation or monomial action depending on group degree (n or n(q−1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When acting on a code, Magma computes action on generators and returns the code generated by images; image-of-code under permutation is isomorphic and under monomial is equivalent. If group degree is neither n nor n(q−1) an error is raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix(C,G) returns subcode fixed by group
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an [n,k] code C and a permutation group G of degree n, Fix(C,G) returns the subcode of C consisting of codewords fixed by every element of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for extracting symmetric subcodes and exploring orbits; G-sets of images can be smaller than group order if images repeat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence vs Isomorphism of codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Two linear codes are equivalent if one may be obtained from the other by a monomial action. They are isomorphic if one may be obtained from the other by a permutation action (permuting coordinate positions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For binary codes equivalence and isomorphism coincide. Use IsEquivalent(C,D) to test monomial equivalence and IsIsomorphic(C,D) to test permutation isomorphism (Magma currently only tests isomorphism for binary codes). If true, the functions return the mapping as a second value.

rubrics_metrics.name: StandardForm does not canonicalise isomorphism classes
rubrics_metrics.description: StandardForm(C) returns a code in standard form that is isomorphic to C, but isomorphic codes need not have the same standard form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume StandardForm(C) yields a unique representative across isomorphism classes; StandardForm(R) may not equal StandardForm(T) even if R and T are isomorphic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphism groups: MonomialGroup / PermutationGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: MonomialGroup(C) or AutomorphismGroup(C) returns the group of all monomial transformations preserving C as a permutation group of degree n(q−1). PermutationGroup(C) returns the group of coordinate permutations mapping C to itself as a permutation group of degree n. Each returns (group, parent M, transfer map t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MonomialGroup gives automorphisms in monomial degree; PermutationGroup is equal to MonomialGroup only for binary codes. Aut(C) returns the parent M and transfer map t; Aut(C,T) selects action type 'Monomial' or 'Permutation'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encoding in standard form and InformationSpace
rubrics_metrics.description: If a code C is in standard form, the information set corresponds to the first k components; encoding a message vector is done by multiplying by GeneratorMatrix(C). Use InformationSpace(C) to get the information space and Coordinates(C,u) to extract the information part of a codeword.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: encoded message equals message * GeneratorMatrix(C) and the encoded is the message followed by check digits when C is in standard form; InformationSet(C) returns the ordered information coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syndrome definition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: The syndrome of a vector relative to a code is zero iff that vector is a codeword. Syndrome(received, C) returns the syndrome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syndrome decoding uses the fact that vectors with the same syndrome lie in the same coset of the code; syndrome non-zero indicates transmission errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syndrome decoding via coset leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetLeaders(C) returns all coset leaders and a map from syndrome space to the ambient space. The coset leader map applied to a syndrome gives the error vector; corrected = received − errorvec; decoded information = InformationSpace!Coordinates(C, corrected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard nearest-neighbour decoding approach; computation of coset leaders can be expensive (number of coset leaders equals number of cosets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of nearest-neighbour decoding (ambiguity)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a received vector is equally distant to two or more codewords, syndrome (nearest-neighbour) decoding may choose the wrong codeword; codes may detect errors they cannot correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a double error may be detected but not corrected by a code designed to correct only single errors; distances to competing codewords should be inspected to understand decoding failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decode(C,v) behaviour and algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Decode attempts to decode v. If successful it returns true and the decoded vector. Two algorithms are available: 'Euclidean' (default for alternant codes) and 'Syndrome' (explicit request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Euclidean decoding is faster and avoids computing coset leaders but cannot correct as many errors as syndrome decoding; for non-alternant codes only syndrome decoding is available. The user can set the parameter Al := 'Syndrome' to force syndrome decoding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euclidean algorithm applicability and error-correction bound
rubrics_metrics.description: The Euclidean decoding algorithm operates on alternant codes (including BCH, Goppa, Reed–Solomon and related) and typically corrects up to floor(r/2) errors for a Goppa code with parameter r (example: r = 3 gives floor(r/2) = 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Euclidean decoding may produce a decoded vector that is not in C in some cases; the user should verify results. Default choice for alternant codes is Euclidean for performance reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulation prerequisites for character-by-character encoding
rubrics_metrics.description: To encode ASCII codes 1..127 character-by-character using codewords, the chosen code must have at least 127 codewords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example uses BCH code with n=15, d=5 (128 codewords), leaving one unused codeword; map unused or non-codewords to placeholder characters when decoding fails or to handle unused indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perturbation (noise) model for simulation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the send simulation, per-coordinate independent perturbation is applied: for each coordinate i, with probability 'noise' the coordinate is altered (incremented modulo field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: noise=0 means perfect transmission; noise near 1 means every component may be altered. If decode flag is true, decoding is applied after perturbation; otherwise non-codewords are mapped to a placeholder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance considerations: syndrome vs Euclidean timing trade-off
rubrics_metrics.description: Syndrome decoding can be much slower than Euclidean decoding when coset leaders are expensive to compute (example timing shown where syndrome decoding took significantly longer than Euclidean decoding for the same instance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For alternant codes prefer Euclidean decoding for speed unless stronger error-correction capability of syndrome decoding is required; coset leaders, once computed, are stored (one-time cost).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IsIsomorphic/IsEquivalent optional parameter AutomorphismGroups
rubrics_metrics.description: IsEquivalent and IsIsomorphic accept a parameter AutomorphismGroups which can be 'None', 'Left', 'Right' (default), or 'Both' to specify which automorphism groups to construct first to potentially speed up isomorphism/equivalence testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing this parameter from default may significantly affect performance for certain examples.
